decisions.executionNote: Raise and pitch both wrists in their own workspaces to view the objects and prepare top-down approaches; category placement will be adapted from live views.
Continue smooth elbow-up approach above the two cameras, pitching grippers down while preserving lateral separation.
Lower toward the two camera bodies with open fingers; use the wrist views to refine the final grasp rather than assume contact.
Close on both camera bodies and lift gently to verify retention. Reserve white for cameras, blue for cars, and red for watches.
Carry the left camera toward the white basket. Bring the right camera to a central tabletop staging point for a later left-arm pickup, without crossing either arm.
Lower and release the first camera inside white; set the second camera on the central table for a non-crossing handoff.
Withdraw open grippers from both released cameras. Move left toward the staged camera and right back into its workspace, leaving room for the handoff pickup.
Approach the staged camera with the left arm and the wooden car with the right, remaining above both objects for wrist-view alignment.
Descend slowly with open fingers toward the central camera and wooden car, making small wrist-image alignment corrections.
Center the fingers on the camera and wooden car, close fully, then lift a short distance to check retention from RGB.
The left camera appears retained; carry it toward white. The wooden car was not retained, so reopen and shift the right approach left/back toward its new center.
The camera slipped onto the table, so reapproach its visible center. Lift and rotate the right wrist to align across the wooden car's narrower dimension before retrying.
Refine both wrist alignments, lower to body height, and close across the camera and the car's narrow waist. Hold position at closure before testing the lift.
Maintain fully closed commands and lift vertically at low speed to verify both grasps before any lateral carrying.
Neither object followed the test lift. Reopen and descend further, correcting the camera centering; inspect finger depth before closing again.
Bring the fingers lower onto the object sides, close fully, and allow the grasp to settle before a very small lift.
Test the deeper grasps with a slow vertical lift while maintaining fully closed commands on both grippers.
Both objects now remain fixed in the wrist views during lifting. Raise clear of the rims and carry the camera toward white and the wooden car toward blue, keeping the arms separated.
Move the retained camera inward over white and the car inward over blue, lowering gradually while keeping both grippers closed.
Replan after the continuity rejection: use smaller right-arm translations, lower before reaching farther, and turn the car inward. Continue the camera's gentle descent over white.
Release the second camera in white and withdraw vertically. Move the wooden car farther inside blue rather than releasing over its front-right rim.
Avoid the right-arm reach boundary by lowering and easing wrist pitch instead of extending farther forward. Retract the left wrist from the completed camera basket.
Release the wooden car inside blue and withdraw the right arm. Approach the remaining turquoise car with the left, aligning the fingers across its width.
Center the turquoise car between the left fingers and approach the silver watch with the right. Lower slowly with open grippers to establish grasp depth.
Lower the left fingers around the car sides and center the right fingers on the watch band. Close fully at the deeper grasp height and pause.
Keep both grippers fully closed, pause briefly, then lift vertically to verify whether the turquoise car and silver watch are retained.
The car and watch have followed the lift. Carry them above rim height toward the left side of blue and the red basket, maintaining closed grippers and arm separation.
Lower the retained turquoise car farther inside blue. The silver watch slipped back onto the table; reopen and reapproach its new location rather than release over red.
Open the left gripper to leave the turquoise car in blue and lift away. Recenter over the silver watch and descend deeper with the right fingers open for a more secure grasp.
Shift the right grasp toward the watch's center after a small clearance lift, then close. Begin withdrawing the unused left arm toward its origin while preserving elbow-up continuity.
Test the centered watch grasp with a straight lift and no wrist rotation. Continue bringing the left arm near its origin with the gripper open.
The watch did not remain fixed during lifting. Reopen and approach lower and slightly back to capture a solid band section rather than the ring's empty center; finish the left-arm return.
Corrected the rejected tensor; no previous motion occurred. Shift the open right fingers forward onto the solid silver band after a small clearance lift.
The silver watch face and band now lie between the fingers. Close at this alignment, pause to settle, and make only a short vertical retention test.
The solid band is now visibly between the closed fingers. Lift gradually and begin moving toward red without rotating the wrist, checking retention before release.
The watch remains fixed in the wrist image. Carry it inside the red basket and lower gradually, maintaining the secure band grasp.
Release the silver watch over the red interior, allow it to settle, then lift and retreat clear of the rim before approaching the remaining green watch.
Approach the remaining green watch from above with the right gripper open. The silver watch is visibly settled in red; both other category baskets remain undisturbed.
Align with the green watch's solid face/band, descend with open fingers, then close and hold before attempting to lift.
Keep the right gripper fully closed and make a short, slow vertical test lift of the green watch without wrist rotation.
The green watch slipped during the test. Reopen, move the finger pads forward onto the solid watch face, and descend for a better-centered grasp.
Center on the green watch's solid face, close fully at the corrected depth, and allow the grasp to settle before a tiny lift.
Test the green watch grasp with a straight slow lift, keeping the fully closed command and watching for any slip relative to the fingers.
The watch remains on the table. Reopen and correct slightly right, then lower the finger pads to the solid watch face instead of pinching beside the band.
The watch face is behind the pinch point in the wrist view. Lift slightly, move back to align with the solid face, lower again, and close without lateral motion.
Maintain full closure long enough to settle the green watch between the pads, then make a two-centimeter test lift without rotating.
The green watch is fixed relative to the pads during the test lift. Raise it clear of the table and start toward red, keeping the wrist orientation and full closure unchanged.
Carry the retained green watch over the red basket at constant height and orientation, leaving the silver watch undisturbed on the left side.
Lower the green watch into the red basket and open the gripper, pausing at release so the watch can settle before withdrawal.
Both watches are visibly released in red. Lift clear of the rim and retract the right arm toward origin with the gripper open, preserving elbow-up continuity.
Return the right wrist smoothly to its original pose with decreasing increments, and correct the small left-arm origin drift. Keep both grippers open while the sorted objects settle.
